title: Presentations of finite filtered bounded below derived categories
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with cochain complexes and $D^+(\mathcal C)$ as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $CF_f^+(\mathcal C)$ be the category of bounded-below cochain complexes with a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration] and [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] such that $F^aK=K$ and $F^bK=0$ for some integers $a,b$ independent of cochain degree. Its morphisms preserve every filtration step, with induced graded maps as in [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction]. Put $W=\{f: \operatorname{gr}^p f\text{ is a quasi-isomorphism for every }p\}$. A presentation of $DF_f^+(\mathcal C)$ is a category $\mathcal D$ with a localization functor $Q:CF_f^+(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal D$ at $W$, equipped with its induced triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] and the descended exact functors $\omega,\operatorname{gr}^p:\mathcal D\to D^+(\mathcal C)$. These functors come with their natural factorizations on complexes and chain maps. The induced triangulation means exactly the triangles isomorphic to the images of filtered cone triangles. A shifted representative has underlying complex $K[1]$ and the shifted filtration. The cone of $f:K\to L$ has underlying complex $C(f)$, filtration $F^p C(f)^n=F^pK^{n+1}\oplus F^pL^n$, and the ordinary cone inclusion and connecting map. The specified localization shift comparisons identify the shifted representative with $(QK)[1]$. For integers $a,b$, write $\operatorname{Supported}_{[a,b]}(M)$ if $\operatorname{gr}^p M=0$ for $p<a$ or $p>b$, where zero means zero in the derived category. On the full pure-degree-$p$ subcategory, the canonical natural comparison $\operatorname{gr}^p M\simeq\omega M$ is normalized on complexes with $F^pK=K$ and $F^{p+1}K=0$ by the subobject inclusion and cokernel projection. Presentations carry this normalized comparison; they supply no lift of any ordinary functor.
